item.revised_prompt: The blue X-shaped line layout in <Picture 1> is <Subject 1>. The four red circular endpoint markers at the tips of the lines in <Picture 1> are <Subject 2>. The target image shows a strict orthographic top-down view of a compact everyday aerial photography quadcopter with its nose oriented toward the top edge, replacing the solid black background and red guide dots of <Picture 1> with a plain light background while matching the arm directions, spacing, and bar widths of <Subject 1> and the motor centers of <Subject 2>. <Subject 1> supplies the exact diagonal arm directions, equal horizontal and vertical spacing, intersection geometry, and arm width transferred to the quadcopter's four unfolded arms. <Subject 2> supplies the exact center positions for the four motors transferred to the quadcopter's motor mounts. The complete product is centered on a clean, uniform off-white studio background with no guide marks or lettering. At the center, a rounded pod features a continuous curved outline that tapers toward the top into an elongated nose shell wrapping smoothly around the internal forward-facing camera; from directly overhead, only the smooth matte light grey top surface of the nose is visible, with no exposed gimbal arms or side lugs. The central body has a plain, unseamed top cover in a uniform matte light grey finish. Four straight arms of uniform width—matching the thickness of the bars in <Subject 1> and arranged along the exact diagonals of <Subject 1> to form a true X with a 250 mm opposite-motor span—grow seamlessly out of the central shell without any root joint lines, sharing the same continuous matte light grey color. Positioned precisely at the four tip locations of <Subject 2>, each cylindrical dark grey motor mount carries a single stationary two-blade, 5-inch matte black propeller with no propeller guards. Soft, even overhead studio lighting casts subtle contact shadows beneath the airframe onto the light background.
